A.explanation: Both are $\text{m s}^{-2}$ because $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N kg}^{-1} = 1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: Both are $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ because $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, the unit of momentum and impulse.

C.explanation: Both are the same because pressure is defined by $p = F/A$, so $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$ by definition.

D.explanation: They differ because $1 \text{ N C}^{-1} = 1 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ for electric field strength, which has an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ compared with $\text{V m}^{-2}$.

hints: Start by writing $1 \text{ N}$ in SI base units as $1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ and use it to test the $\text{N kg}^{-1}$, $\text{N s}$ and $\text{N m}^{-2}$ pairs.
Recall that electric field strength $E = F/q$ has unit $\text{N C}^{-1}$ and also $E = V/d$ has unit $\text{V m}^{-1}$, so check what power of metre each side of pair D contains.
Compare $\text{V m}^{-2}$ with $\text{V m}^{-1}$: if one side reduces to field strength and the other has an extra division by metre, they cannot be the same in base units.
walkthrough: Write the newton in base units from $F = ma$: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$. This lets you test each pair.
For $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $\text{N kg}^{-1}$: $\text{N kg}^{-1} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}\text{kg}^{-1} = \text{m s}^{-2}$, so they match.
For $\text{N s}$ and $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$: $\text{N s} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{s} = \text{kg m s}^{-1}$, so they match.
For $\text{Pa}$ and $\text{N m}^{-2}$: $\text{Pa}$ is defined as pressure $= \text{force/area}$, so $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$ exactly.

For $\text{V m}^{-2}$ and $\text{N C}^{-1}$: electric field $E = F/q$ gives $\text{N C}^{-1}$, and $E = V/d$ gives $\text{V m}^{-1}$. Hence $\text{N C}^{-1}$ is equivalent to $\text{V m}^{-1}$, not $\text{V m}^{-2}$.
Therefore only the pair with $\text{V m}^{-2}$ and $\text{N C}^{-1}$ are not the same. This is option D.
